# A tiny contained endpoint has exact mixed simplex depth

Let T be a full-dimensional d-simplex of volume V and centroid g.
Here mu is the sum of d-dimensional Lebesgue measures on the
actual integer fibers, A_mu(y)=inf_{H contains y} mu(H) uses all
closed ambient halfspaces with nonzero normal, and normalized
depth is A_mu(y)/mu(S). All candidate points belong to S.
For every d>=2 there is a proved dimension-only constant rho_d>0
such that the following holds for EVERY compact convex A subset T
with volume 0<a<=rho_d V. Put A,T,T at integer bases -1,0,1.
The resulting actual convex source has exact maximum absolute depth

    D_mix=Gamma_d V+a,
    Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.                              (1)

Its UNIQUE global maximizing point is (0,g). No diameter, shape,
centroid or rate hypothesis on the small set A is imposed.
The proof uses one common oblique halfspace throughout.

The dimension-only threshold is an explicit compact scalar-profile
minimum, proved strictly positive below. In dimension two it equals

    rho_2=2(sqrt(10)-3)/9                             (2)

for this sufficient profile criterion. We do not claim that this
is the largest possible mass range for the actual geometric theorem.

## 1. A continuous cap profile and its positive minimum

For a unit continuous normal u write

    b(u)=u.g, ell(u)=min_{x in T}u.x,
    f(u)=|T intersect {u.x>=b(u)}|/V,
    q(u)=|T intersect {u.x>=2b(u)-ell(u)}|/V.

Define

    rho_d=min_{|u|=1}[f(u)-Gamma_d+q(u)].             (3)

All terms are continuous on the sphere. For q this remains true
when its threshold becomes a supporting level or moves beyond T:
every hyperplane has zero d-volume and bounded convergence applies.
Ordinary Grunbaum gives f>=Gamma_d. By its simplex equality
classification, recorded in
candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c, equality
occurs precisely at the d+1 canonical apex-side facet-parallel
directions. At such a direction use its barycentric coordinate
lambda_i. Then ell=0, b=1/(d+1), and

    q=((d-1)/(d+1))^d>0  for d>=2.                   (4)

Hence the nonnegative continuous expression in (3) cannot vanish
anywhere. Compactness proves rho_d>0. Its value is unchanged by
an invertible affine transformation of T: the cap fractions and
the reflected threshold transform together, and all directions
are retained. Thus it depends only on d.

For a coefficient-only specification, normalize a nonconstant
affine functional at the vertices to values r_0,...,r_d in [0,1]
with min r_i=0 and max r_i=1. Put bar r=sum r_i/(d+1), and let
Phi_r(s) be the tail probability of sum r_i lambda_i for uniform
simplex barycentrics. Equivalently,

    Phi_r(s)=[r_0,...,r_d](x-s)_+^d,

using confluent divided differences at repeated nodes. This tail
identity is proved in the archived simplex slice/cap calculus.
There is no all-equal knot vector in the compact domain. Formula
(3) is exactly the minimum of

    Phi_r(bar r)+Phi_r(2bar r)-Gamma_d                (5)

on that explicitly specified compact set. Thus (3) is a fixed
simplex directional constant, not an unproved mixed-depth lemma.

## 2. One coupled endpoint inequality for every actual tilt

Fix a nonvertical ambient halfspace through (0,g), written

    H={u.(x-g)+beta z>=0}.

Let c=b(u)-beta be its threshold in the +1 copy of T. Its threshold
in the -1 copy A is exactly 2b(u)-c. If c<=2b(u)-ell(u), the +1
cap has volume at least q(u)V. If c>2b(u)-ell(u), the -1 threshold
is strictly below ell(u), so it captures ALL A. Thus, for every
beta and every A subset T,

    |A intersect H_-1|+|T intersect H_1|
                    >=min(a,q(u)V).                 (6)

At equality of the two thresholds A is also fully captured,
including its closed boundary; either branch gives the same valid
lower bound. This is the actual affine coupling of the two source
thresholds. They have not been minimized independently.

Set alpha=a/V<=rho_d. Adding the actual middle cap to (6) gives

    mu(H)/V>=f(u)+min(alpha,q(u))>=Gamma_d+alpha.     (7)

Indeed, if q>=alpha use f>=Gamma_d. Otherwise use
f+q>=Gamma_d+rho_d>=Gamma_d+alpha. This proves the lower bound
for all nonvertical through-point caps simultaneously.

A vertical through-point cap contains the whole middle fiber and
at least one endpoint. Its mass is at least V+a (as a<=V), which
also exceeds Gamma_d V+a. Any containing cap includes a parallel
through-point cap, so (7) proves the full closed-halfspace lower
bound at the single actual point (0,g).

## 3. Actual convex compatibility and a finite exact upper cover

The convex hull of the three lifted bodies has exactly A,T,T as
its integer fibers. The endpoints are extreme projection fibers,
and (A+T)/2 subset T prevents any middle enlargement. There are
no other integer bases. It is a full-dimensional ambient body,
and every real fiber contains A. Any point of int A therefore
also supplies a common interior continuous section.

Let lambda_0,...,lambda_d be the barycentric coordinates of T,
and m=d+1. The following 2m ORIGINAL ambient caps form a finite
cover of the entire actual mixed source:

    P_i={lambda_i(x)-2z>=1/m},
    Q_i={lambda_i(x)+2(z-1)>=1/m},  i=0,...,d.        (8)

At base zero the P_i form the canonical cover of T; they fully
capture A at base -1 and strictly exclude the +1 copy of T.
Each has mass exactly Gamma_d V+a. At base +1 the Q_i form its
canonical cover; they strictly exclude both other fibers. Each
has mass Gamma_d V. The signs follow from 0<=lambda_i<=1 on
both A and T. Thus (8) proves the global upper bound in (1).

For uniqueness, at any middle point y different from g one has
lambda_i(y)>1/m for some i. The cap

    {lambda_i(x)-2z>=lambda_i(y)}

has mass V(1-lambda_i(y))^d+a<Gamma_d V+a. At a +1 point choose
an index with lambda_i(y)>=1/m and use the analogous isolated
Q_i with that threshold, giving at most Gamma_d V. Any -1 point
has the vertical isolating cap z<=-1 of mass a. All are strictly
below (1). Hence no other source point maximizes depth.

All coefficients in these upper certificates are finite and
explicit. Coverage is asserted over the three actual integer
fiber spaces, not over every real base after isolation.

## 4. Exact planar evaluation of the profile threshold

For d=2, permutation and affine normalization reduce every
direction to vertex values (0,r,1), 0<=r<=1. Its mean is
(1+r)/3. Direct triangle cap areas give the profile in (5) as

    (5r^2-4r+1)/(9(1-r)),       0<=r<=1/2,
    (3-r-1/r)/9,                1/2<=r<=1.           (9)

For the first interval both thresholds are in the top vertex-cap
regime. For the second, the own cap is the complement of the
bottom vertex cap and the reflected threshold is at or beyond
the top support. The endpoint expressions in (9) agree at 1/2.

Putting v=1-r in the first expression gives
(5v+2/v-6)/9. AM-GM yields its minimum
(2sqrt(10)-6)/9, attained at v=sqrt(2/5), which lies in [1/2,1].
The second expression increases on [1/2,1], with minimum 1/18.
The former value is strictly smaller because sqrt(10)<13/4.
This proves (2), with no numerical normal screen.

## 5. Exact mixed versus projected first variations

The normalized mixed maximum in (1) is exactly

    (Gamma_d+alpha)/(2+alpha)
       =Gamma_d/2+alpha(2-Gamma_d)/4+O(alpha^2).      (10)

Thus the derivative of the maximum absolute mixed depth with
respect to the added endpoint mass is exactly ONE, regardless
of how the subsets A shrink or change shape within T.

For comparison, take the thin E_epsilon from
candidate 7ff8cebaefda7361
as A. Its projected ordinary law is 2 1_T+1_Eepsilon. That note
proves the derivative of its maximum absolute projected depth
with respect to |Eepsilon| is 1/(d+1), and its normalized ordinary
depth decreases. Here (10) gives a strictly increasing normalized
mixed depth from the two-fiber mixed baseline. The two measures
and their halfspace classes are kept distinct in this comparison.

## 6. A separate one-dimensional calibration

Formula (3) gives rho_1=0, so its proof does not supply an interval
threshold. There is nevertheless a separate exact argument in
d=1, valid for every positive interval A subset T.

Reflect A through the midpoint g of T. The interval 2g-A is still
contained in T. The retained three-fiber source A,T,2g-A is
centrally symmetric about (0,g), of mass V+2a. Every closed
through-point halfspace therefore captures at least V/2+a.
The upper cover (8), with Gamma_1=1/2, gives equality, and the
same uniqueness argument applies. This proves the d=1 statement
independently, rather than inserting a positive constant into (3).

The result concerns this particular three-fiber contained-endpoint
class. It does not assert a general three-fiber theorem or a
variational reduction of arbitrary OC failures to this class.

## 7. Exact one-extra-fiber law over a binary simplex core

The same local law extends to every integer dimension n>=1.
Put an identical T at every base in {0,1}^n. Choose distinct cube
vertices q,v and append A at p=2q-v, with A subset T and the same
mass range as above. The resulting actual convex source has

    max A_mu=Gamma_d V+a,
    max depth_mu=(Gamma_d+alpha)/(2^n+alpha),          (11)

and its unique maximizing point is (q,g). For d>=2 assume
alpha<=rho_d; for d=1 the separate interval proof permits all
0<alpha<=1. The normalized right derivative at alpha=0 is
(2^n-Gamma_d)/4^n>0.

The first-shell integer-support classification is already proved
in candidate 8a123edc8f6439bd; the short
special-case argument is included here to make the exact-depth
certificate self-contained. The new conclusion is the exact
maximum and unique center, rather than that support classification.

Here are the full integer and cap details. Integer-preserving
coordinate flips first send q to 0, v to 1_I and p to -1_I,
where I is a nonempty coordinate set and k=|I|. Every coordinate
of conv({0,1}^n union {p}) lies in [-1,1], or in [0,1] outside I.
An integer point outside the cube must have a coordinate -1.
In a convex representation this forces all weight onto p, because
every cube vertex has that coordinate at least zero. Thus the
exact integer support is the cube union {p}.

All continuous generators lie in T. Each original cube fiber is
therefore still exactly T; the exposed fiber at p is exactly A.
The lifted hull is full dimensional, with no additional integer
fiber or lattice normalization assumption.

Restrict any ambient halfspace through (q,g) to the line through
p,q,v. Its three traces have the single scalar affine tilt in
Section 2, so those three fibers alone pay Gamma_d V+a. This
proves the lower bound regardless of the other cube fibers.

For the upper bound at q=0 use delta_q(z)=sum_i z_i. It is zero
at q, at least one at every other cube vertex, and equals -k at p.
The caps

    {lambda_i(x)-2 delta_q(z)>=1/(d+1)}

each capture the own canonical T cap and ALL A, and exclude all
other cube fibers. They have mass Gamma_d V+a.

Every other cube vertex w remains exposed. Explicitly set

    delta_w(z)=(k+1) sum_{i:w_i=1}(1-z_i)
                         +sum_{i:w_i=0} z_i.

It vanishes at w and is at least one at other cube vertices.
If j=|I intersect supp(w)| and s=|supp(w) minus I|, then

    delta_w(p)=(2k+3)j+(k+1)s-k>=1,

because w is nonzero. Hence the same finite coefficient 2 in
{lambda_i(x)-2 delta_w(z)>=1/(d+1)} isolates each such canonical
cap, with budget Gamma_d V. Together with the q group these
original caps cover the entire actual source, including A.

At a noncentroid point of q, increase the appropriate canonical
threshold to lambda_i(y)>1/(d+1), giving strictly smaller mass
than (11). At a different cube point its isolated own cap gives
at most Gamma_d V. Finally delta_p(z)=sum_{i in I}z_i+k vanishes
only at p and is positive on the cube, so the vertical cap
delta_p<=0 gives mass a. These bounds prove uniqueness.

This is an exact local allocation law for an identical-simplex
binary core with one contained added fiber. It is not a statement
about arbitrary parity cores or multiple added fibers.

## 8. Separate centrally symmetric-body calibration

Let K be any full-dimensional centrally symmetric convex body in
R^d, with center g and volume V. Let A subset K be any positive
convex body of volume a, with no smallness requirement beyond
a<=V. The same binary-core construction has exact maximum

    max A_mu=V/2+a,
    max depth_mu=(1/2+alpha)/(2^n+alpha),             (12)

again uniquely at (q,g).

Indeed, on the reflected triple p,q,v retain A,K,2g-A. This is
an actual submeasure centrally symmetric about (q,g), of mass
V+2a. Every closed through-point halfspace therefore captures at
least V/2+a. The other source fibers can only add mass.

For a finite upper cover, choose d independent continuous linear
directions u and their negatives, and normalize the corresponding
affine functionals phi_u on K to have range [0,1]. Symmetry gives
phi_u(g)=1/2 and every cap {phi_u>=1/2} has volume V/2. Their
union covers K. Replace each barycentric lambda_i in the isolated
caps of Section 7 by these phi_u and replace 1/(d+1) by 1/2.
All isolation signs remain valid because A subset K and each
phi_u has range [0,1]. The q caps have mass V/2+a, and the other
cube caps have mass V/2. They form a finite cover of the actual
source, including A.

If y is in K and y!=g, take a direction u with u.(y-g)>0.
The cap {u.x>=u.y} has volume strictly below V/2: it removes a
positive-volume slab from the half of K at g. Positivity follows
from g in int K, even if y lies on its boundary. The same finite
base tilt isolates this cap at q while including at most all A,
so its mixed mass is strictly less than V/2+a. All other cube
points have isolated own caps of mass at most V/2, and p has its
vertical cap of mass a. This proves uniqueness.

This is a separate reflection argument. For d>1 its coefficient
1/2 differs from Gamma_d; it does not give a positive value for
the reflected-threshold profile (3) in centrally symmetric bodies.

## 9. Exact verification scope

../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_tiny_contained_endpoint_exact_mixed_depth.py uses only the
Python standard library. It checks the planar profile identity
at 101 rational directions, 5304 actual coupled planar cap
instances, the finite canonical cover budgets, and 33537 binary
isolation inequalities, as well as the all-dimensional canonical
positivity in (4). The compact positivity proof, its exact planar
minimum, and all-dimension geometric arguments above are analytic;
the finite checks are auxiliary rather than substitutes for them.
